examples.input: Save a file in an editor that empties the file first and then writes the new content

results.1: nothing is recorded while the file is empty; the software records the file once it reads the same on two checks in a row, with the full new content
results.2: the empty file may be recorded as the latest version, and the full content is recorded only on a later pass, if it is noticed at all

context.in_practice: Route 1 adds a short wait after each change and accepts a file only once it has stopped changing. A file that keeps changing, such as a growing log, may be picked up late or not until it goes quiet. Route 2 was not considered as an alternative. In practice it means acting on the file the moment a change is seen, which is faster but trusts whatever is on disk at that instant.
context.stakes: If a file is picked up while an editor is partway through saving it, the software can record an empty or half-written version as if the user meant it. That can overwrite good data or trigger needless follow-up work.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 costs a small delay and repeated reads before each file is recorded. Route 2 costs the risk of recording empty or half-saved files.

plan_why: The routes differ only in timing: whether `watch` waits until a file being saved reads the same on consecutive checks before reconciling. Showing that needs a running `watch` and a file changing at the same moment (an editor emptying and rewriting it). Commands here run one after another, `watch` is not allowed, and every file is fully written before any command starts. So each command's reconcile sees a settled file and both routes record the same events.
routes: Reconcile only after the bytes read the same on consecutive checks
